The class-advised net discretizes admissible summaries only to \(n^{-1/2}\) accuracy, while the no-advice lattice constructs an outer \(W_1\)-ball rather than the exact image; consequently neither result yields the exact image or its exact support-dependent extrema.

open_obligations.partial_result:
The computable surrogate and the auxiliary benchmark are complete.  By \(\mathrm{thm:polynomial\text{-}net\text{-}law\text{-}estimator}\), the class-advised estimator \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\) is a total positive real-law-valued Borel map and satisfies
\[
W_1(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}},\nu_P)\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\{2d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}\},
\]
so the abstract gap-free modulus alone yields collision-uniform root-\(n\) estimation from a precomputed admissible-summary net.  Independently, \(\mathrm{prop:polynomial\text{-}net\text{-}law\text{-}estimator}\) makes \(\widehat\lambda_n\) a no-advice total positive real-law-valued estimator obtained by exhaustive minimization over a structured lattice of cardinality polynomial in \(n\) for fixed \(k,d_x,d_z\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:honest\text{-}root\text{-}n\text{-}confidence}\), \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) is honest and has \(W_1\)-diameter at most \(2R_{n,\alpha}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:cluster\text{-}report}\) and \(\mathrm{thm:cluster\text{-}adaptive\text{-}report}\), every interval \(I_C\) and the full report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) have explicit fixed-dimensional constrained-program representations with the stated support and mass guarantees.  Thus the no-advice lattice dominates the advised net for the operative K1--K4 computational deliverable, and an evaluable honest outer set and report exist even when the raw empirical operator has nonreal eigenpairs.  Only exact computation of the original sharper summary-inversion image and its exact extrema remains unresolved.

prose_updates.tldr: On a uniformly conditioned causal VMW submodel, the primary theorem is a gap-free Lipschitz modulus from the observable moment summary to the positive quotient latent-effect law in \(W_1\), uniform through simultaneous effect merges and splits. Root-\(n\) estimation, honest root-\(n\)-diameter confidence sets, and a cluster report with explicit true-cluster association follow from that modulus. Same-class minimax corollaries give root-\(n\) quotient-law risk and effect-ordered weight risk \(\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,\delta)^{-1}\}\), using factorization-preserving pairs on an explicit full-rank unequal-weight two-class witness. Each converse also transfers to any published-VMW comparator class containing its exact two-point witness pair; no containment of an entire local neighborhood is required. The quotient collision point belongs to the published structural/finite-regularity model but lies outside the separated Theorem 7.2 recovery class, whereas the labeled pair is separated. An auxiliary class-advised admissible-summary net shows independently that the abstract modulus yields a positive collision-uniform root-\(n\) estimator, but the operative K1--K4 computational construction is the no-advice structured lattice and its outer report. Exact polynomial-time computation of the original sharp summary-inversion image remains open. The modulus, estimator uppers, confidence and cluster guarantees, and matching-minimax conclusions remain restricted to the stated uniformly conditioned classes.

project_justification.fill: The paper makes the positive-measure \(W_1\) modulus the root theorem on a uniformly conditioned causal VMW submodel, derives total root-\(n\) estimation, honest root-\(n\)-diameter sets and well-posed cluster reports, and calibrates same-class quotient-law and labeled-weight minimax risk using observed-Kullback--Leibler pairs that preserve the proxy factorization.  A class-advised admissible-summary net records the independent abstract modulus-to-estimation benchmark, while the no-advice structured lattice is the operative K1--K4 computational deliverable and supports the evaluable outer confidence set and report.  Exact computation of the original sharp summary-inversion image is left as a separate residual question.  The lower bounds transfer further to precisely those published-VMW comparator classes containing the corresponding two witness laws; whole-neighborhood containment is unnecessary, while all upper and inference guarantees retain their narrower class scope.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The published VMW boundedness conditions are imposed separately on \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\). Armwise empirical moments divide by \(\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}\), are zero on empty arms, and combine with \(n^{-1}\sum_iX_i\) to form \(\widehat S_n\). The theoretical route applies Borel nearest-summary projection and \(\overline F\). An auxiliary class-advised route searches a precomputed \(n^{-1/2}\)-net of admissible summaries and witnesses the abstract modulus-to-estimation reduction. The operative computable route minimizes an explicit no-advice finite structured lattice, never diagonalizes the raw empirical operator, and supplies the outer confidence set and cluster report.

prose_updates.related_work: Virk, Mazaheri, and Wu (2026, Theorem 5.4, Proposition 6.2, Assumption 4, and Theorem 7.2) provide the population operator-moment identity and the known homogeneity reduction.  In their fixed-dimensional finite-sample regime, Assumption 4 imposes finite almost-sure envelopes for \(X\), \(ZX^\top\), and \(YZX^\top\), positive marginal treatment-arm probability, and a positive population singular-value margin; its other named constants are derived conditioning quantities.  Theorem 7.2 additionally assumes proxy richness, strict latent positivity, pairwise-distinct treatment effects when \(k\ge2\), and its stated sample-dependent radius conditions before delivering high-probability treatment-effect, anchor-normalized feature-matrix, and simplex-projected mixture-weight recovery.  Their structural/finite-regularity model contains the explicit quotient collision pair because it retains full proxy rank and strict positivity without requiring distinct effects, but the collision point is outside that separated recovery theorem; the labeled witness pair is separated. Consequently, the two Le Cam converses transfer to any published-VMW comparator class containing the corresponding exact pair, with no need for whole-neighborhood containment. The gap-free positive-law modulus, estimator uppers, confidence and cluster guarantees, and matching-minimax conclusions remain on the explicitly narrower uniformly conditioned causal submodel. Mazaheri, Squires, and Uhler (2025) identify a finite latent-effect mixture through scalar synthetic moments and a Hankel pencil, without collision-uniform inference. Bauer and Fike (1960) localize spectra of perturbed diagonalizable operators, while Kato (1995, Chapter II) supplies contour-defined aggregate projectors for externally isolated clusters; neither result assigns positive causal spectral masses through a merge. Wu and Yang (2020, Sections 1, 4, and 5) project noisy summaries onto a feasible moment space before positive atomic extraction in Gaussian mixture deconvolution and inform the repair handle. Heinrich and Kahn (2018, Sections 3--5) and Ho and Nguyen (2016) analyze collision singularities for ordinary mixtures, not factorization-preserving pairs in the VMW observed proxy experiment. Polyanskiy and Wu (2019) develop Le Cam two-point and dual functional-estimation lower bounds and elbow phenomena, whereas \(\mathrm{thm:matching\text{-}local\text{-}lower\text{-}bounds}\) supplies explicit factorization-preserving observed-data pairs tailored to the proxy-causal model. Deo and Randrianarisoa (2023), Robins and van der Vaart (2006), and Bing, Bunea, and Niles-Weed (2025) inform the confidence-set architecture but do not treat multiplicity of a nonnormal causal operator. Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018) motivate proxy conditional-independence and rank discipline. Van Amsterdam et al. (2022) provide the PROTECT stage-III NSCLC consumer, conditional on a separate finite-fitness and censoring bridge; their hazard model is not claimed to lie in \(\mathcal M\). Brown and Purves (1973) supply the measurable-extrema selection theorem used to choose a Borel nearest point in the compact feasible-summary closure.
prose_updates.interpretation: The regular inferential object is the quotient law, not an effect-ordered labeling of latent classes. When effects collide, both the class-advised net benchmark and the no-advice lattice estimator operate at root-\(n\) scale, but only the latter is the operative K1--K4 computational construction. The cluster report merges coordinates unresolved at radius \(R_{n,\alpha}/m_\star\) and reports their aggregate mass; only externally separated clusters receive sharper coordinate interpretation. The theoretical image set and computable outer set are both honest but are not asserted equal or nested, and neither available estimator computes the original exact summary-inversion image.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The analytic collision bottleneck is settled by the gap-free positive-measure modulus, including simultaneous merges and splits and nonreal raw empirical spectra after feasible-summary projection. The explicit factorization-preserving calculations also settle the two local lower-bound orders. The remaining open issue is computational rather than statistical: nearest projection and exact inversion of the continuum feasible-summary set may be expensive, and \(\mathrm{oeq:constructive\text{-}total\text{-}repair}\) asks whether the original sharp summary-inversion image can be computed exactly in polynomial time in the fixed-dimensional exact-real model. The auxiliary finite-library net theorem gives a class-advised polynomial-online-time root-\(n\) estimator directly from the abstract modulus, independently of the structured parametrization. It is not the operative K1--K4 computational deliverable and is dominated there by \(\mathrm{prop:polynomial\text{-}net\text{-}law\text{-}estimator}\), whose no-advice structured lattice also supports the computable outer confidence set and cluster report. Neither construction computes the exact sharp image.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The law-level theorems fix and know \(k,d_x,d_z\), use the exact VMW observable conditional independences, and impose two explicitly new uniform-conditioning conditions: a lower bound on every joint latent-arm probability and singular-value margins for \(A_0,A_1,B\). These conditions imply \(P(T=t)\ge k\pi_0\) and, under the conditional normalization of \(M_t(P)\), \(\sigma_k(M_t(P))\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2\); the converse inclusion and gap-free resolution of the full VMW class are not claimed. The displayed potential-outcome and effect envelopes are derived from the retained proxy rank, observable envelopes, separation, consistency, armwise ignorability, and latent--arm positivity conditions; no separate compact-support assumption is imposed. The two-sided \(g\)-window is an additional local-regime shell used only for labeled weights. Population identification and the homogeneous identities \(\Delta Q(P)=\tau_\star I_k\) and \(\nu_P=\delta_{\tau_\star}\) are published VMW background. Each lower bound transfers to any published-VMW comparator class containing its exact two-point witness pair, but no whole-neighborhood containment is required and no gap-free modulus, estimator upper, confidence, cluster, or matching-minimax result transfers with it. The quotient collision point is in the published structural/finite-regularity model but outside the separated Theorem 7.2 recovery class; the labeled pair is separated. The class-advised admissible-summary net is only an auxiliary modulus-to-estimation benchmark; the no-advice structured lattice supplies the operative computational estimator and outer report, while exact polynomial-time computation of the original sharp image remains unresolved. Recovery of latent labels at equality and unknown \(k\) also remain outside the settled scope. PROTECT remains a conditional consumer until a separate theorem maps a prespecified finite fitness stratification and bounded censoring-adjusted outcome into the VMW moment model.
